phase_rule: Replace only the phase seed in the corresponding nine83 direction. Use both seeds independently at every listed amplitude, producing six new observations. The clean reference, frequency, curvature, amplitude and [0,1] clipping use the historical generator.
gain_comparison: Measure a=<observed-output,observed-clean>/||observed-clean||^2. Compare raw gains and flag comparable if |a_current-a_previous| <= 0.02. For a_previous>1e-8 also scale the full previous removal by a_current/a_previous, without clipping the analytical reconstruction; evaluate whole image, six peak pairs and aligned-gain excess in exactly the same subspace. Always report missing comparisons or regressions.
primary: On each of three known cases, at comparable gain, compare each of its previously harmed peak pairs to the previous restoration and the previous restoration scaled to the current gain; also compare to noisy input. Report every other peak and the other nine historical recoveries with the same measurements. No aggregate can override a per-peak regression.
squared_error_reporting: Use raw values and absolute tolerance 1e-18 for peak-MSE direction counts (FFT roundoff); whole-image MSE ties use 1e-12. Each disk of radius two FFT bins and its conjugate uses the same reference-selected peaks, normalized by all image pixels. Same-gain excess is removal minus a times actual injected signal.
controls: All 33 clean historical controls (including unclipped and exposure-clipped same-photo variants), their changed-pixel counts, prior nine carries, the full 148 historical inputs with hash replay, and all ten default/alternative-gain 69022 edge checks from nine83. Separately report the six new phases and remaining stripe.
scope: Register before changing the candidate or generating new phases. The three target inputs are design cases; the extra phases come from the same photograph and are only run after code freeze. Retain unsuccessful and unchanged cases.
